research_question: What is the effect of indicated suicide-prevention interventions (targeting young people up to age 25 who already show early signs or symptoms of risk, such as current suicidal ideation or a history of self-harm), compared with control conditions, on suicidal ideation measured immediately at the end of the intervention (postintervention), in education settings (schools, colleges, universities)?
treatment_label: Indicated intervention for young people already showing signs/symptoms of suicide risk, delivered in an education setting
control_label: Control condition (no intervention, waitlist, treatment-as-usual, attention/active control, or usual school curriculum)
outcome_description: Suicidal ideation severity/frequency measured immediately at the end of the intervention (postintervention assessment only), using validated self-report or interview measures such as the Suicidal Ideation Questionnaire (SIQ/SIQ-JR), Beck Scale for Suicide Ideation (BSS/BSSI), Columbia-Suicide Severity Rating Scale ideation items, Positive and Negative Suicide Ideation Inventory, Suicidal Behaviors Questionnaire ideation items, or suicidal-ideation subscales/items of broader instruments (e.g. CES-D item, Youth Risk Behavior Survey ideation item). Short-term (1-3 month), medium-term (4-12 month), and longest-follow-up assessments are NOT part of this outcome. Multi-arm trials contribute one row per indicated-intervention arm against the shared control group. Where only a total N is reported for a randomized trial, an even 50/50 split across groups is assumed and the assumption is noted.
positive_direction: A positive Hedges g / SMD means the indicated intervention produced a GREATER REDUCTION in suicidal ideation at postintervention than the control condition (i.e. lower ideation scores in the intervention group = better outcome).

school-based intervention suicidal ideation self-harm students controlled trial outcome

youth suicidal ideation targeted intervention education setting quantitative outcome
inclusion_criteria: Participants are young people up to approximately age 25 who already show early signs or symptoms of suicide risk (e.g. current or recent suicidal ideation, prior suicide attempt, self-harm history, elevated screening scores), i.e. an indicated-prevention sample

Evaluates an intervention delivered in or through an education setting (school, alternative school, college, university, or education-linked service) and compares it with some form of control or comparison condition

Reports any quantitative suicidal ideation outcome assessed at or near the immediate end of the intervention (postintervention), in a form that allows an effect size to be computed (means and SDs, t/F, proportions, odds ratios, or change scores)
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, editorials, commentaries, opinion pieces, protocols, qualitative-only and purely theoretical papers)
No comparison between an indicated intervention condition and a control/comparison condition (e.g. single-arm pre-post studies with no control group)
No quantitative suicidal ideation outcome data from which an effect size can be derived (no means+SDs, t/F values, proportions, or odds ratios reported or obtainable)

Completely unrelated to the research topic (e.g. adult-only clinical samples, purely universal or selective prevention with no symptomatic subgroup, non-education settings only, or outcomes containing no suicidal ideation measure)
moderators_to_extract: Education setting type (primary/secondary school vs college/university)
Intervention modality (CBT/DBT-based, psychoeducation, skills training, gatekeeper/counselling, digital/online)
Control condition type (waitlist/no treatment vs active or treatment-as-usual)
Mean participant age and age band
Risk-indicator used for inclusion (current ideation vs self-harm/attempt history vs screening score)
Sample size category and study design (RCT vs quasi-experimental)
effect_size_note: Pool as standardized mean difference (SMD, Hedges g bias-corrected), as requested. Sign effect sizes so that a positive value favours the indicated intervention (lower suicidal ideation). Only the postintervention assessment contributes; later follow-ups are excluded from this outcome. Multi-arm trials: each indicated-intervention arm is entered as a separate row against the shared control group (the shared control n may be split or variance-adjusted at analysis to avoid double-counting). For randomized trials reporting only a total N, assume an even 50/50 group split and flag the assumption in the extraction notes.
